Summary: Harborline runs containerized route-optimization and document ingestion for manifest/BL processing. Very sensitive to tail latency for chat workflows used by ops. Commercial ask: reserved capacity for peak shipping loads (weekday morning batch + on-demand chat during port arrivals).

Key call highlights:
- 2026-03-03 kickoff: Product + infra review. Customer asked for 99.99% uptime and strict maintenance windows (only Sundays 0200-0400 local).
- 2026-03-10 SLA deep-dive w/ legal + infra. Redwood proposed 99.95% with credit tiers; Harborline pushed back: wants 99.99 or larger credits.
- POC scheduled: 2-week stress test (throughput + failover) starting 2026-03-18. SE to run synthetic load and KV-cache warm-up scenarios.

Quotes / paraphrases: "We need predictable throughput during peak discharges — sub-second median response for the chat agent or ops will escalate." — Head of Platform.

Commercial posture: risk-averse, price-sensitive vs uptime. Likely to commit to 12+ month reserved contract if SLA + support response times meet their bar.

Internal ask: provide tight maintenance/time windows and explicit credit schedule examples; include peering cost estimate and network egress modeling.
recent_activity: 2026-03-12 follow-up: Redwood provided SLA redline v1
sla_summary: Customer requested uptime: 99.99% (target). Redwood initial offer: 99.95% with graduated credits. Proposed credit schedule discussed: <99.95 = 10% monthly credit; <99.9 = 30% credit; <99.5 = 100% credit and termination clause. Harborline: wants 99.99 floor with larger credits or usage rebates. Maintenance windows: customer requests 2 hours/month, preferred Sundays 02:00-04:00 local; Redwood proposes monthly 4-hour window with 72-hour notice. Support SLA: P1 response 15 minutes phone + 1 hour engineer assignment; P2 1 hour; P3 4 business hours. Harborline pushing for guaranteed phone escalation path and named escalation engineer for first 6 months.
technical_requirements: Throughput: baseline throughput guarantee 200 QPS for small chat requests (<=512 tokens) during reserved window, burstable to 350 QPS for 30 minutes. Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end <300ms for single-turn chat (512 tokens) and p99 <850ms. Reserved GPU planning: initial reserved pool 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs, autoscale headroom to +4 GPUs for bursts; KV-cache pinned per customer; local KV warm-up time target <120s. Model preferences: open Llama-family variant or quantized OPT-variants; fallback routing to smaller quantized model if capacity constrained. Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-request trace id, and audit logs retained 1 year. Data residency: US-only, VPC peering required.
commercial_terms_discussed: Monthly reserved billing with quarterly true-up
Burst billing for capacity above reserved
